title: The Silence of Anderlecht
premise: Edmund Reyes, once a celebrated pianist who abandoned the stage after a catastrophic debut, returns to the Brussels conservatory of Anderlecht as a janitor, sweeping the halls where his family's musical dynasty was made and broken. At his estranged grandmother's funeral, a stranger named Ilse recognizes him by 'Vandenberg' — a name his mother buried — and reveals she is the illegitimate daughter of Edmund's uncle, entitled to a share of the family's decaying house and its locked music room. As Edmund helps Ilse claim her inheritance, he must confront the night his career ended and the duty that silenced three generations. In the end, Edmund opens the music room, gives Ilse the house, and plays again — not as a prodigy reclaiming glory, but as a man finally choosing love over legacy.
about_author: Mara Joubert is a former translator of Dutch and French literature who spent a decade in Brussels before moving to the Flemish coast to write. Her work explores quiet lives interrupted by inheritance, memory, and music.

chapters.title: The Man with the Mop
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund cleans the Anderlecht conservatory at dawn, invisible among students who don't know he once performed on this stage. He tends the building like a penance. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked by small recognitions — a poster of his own debut still framed in a corridor.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At his grandmother Margriet's funeral, a woman in an ill-fitting black coat approaches and calls him 'Vandenberg.' She is Ilse, and she knows things about the family Edmund thought were dead. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past addressing him directly for the first time in fifteen years.

chapters.title: The House on Rue de Fiennes
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse narrates her discovery: letters proving she is the daughter of Edmund's uncle Tomas, raised abroad, now claiming her share of the crumbling family house. She asks Edmund, as the only Reyes who answers letters, to help her enter it. Emotional beat: cautious hope between two strangers bound by other people's secrets.

chapters.title: What the Mother Buried
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund confronts his mother, Anouk, who forbids him from helping Ilse and refuses to say why the Vandenberg name was abandoned. He learns Tomas didn't just leave — he was erased. Emotional beat: anger curdling into doubt about every story he was raised on.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. With a lawyer's letter, Ilse and Edmund open the house. Dust, sheet music, a piano under sheets like a shroud. They find a locked door at the end of the upstairs hall — the music room — and no key. Emotional beat: intimacy growing through shared excavation; grief with company.

chapters.title: The Debut
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, in flashback interleaved with present. The night fifteen years ago: Edmund froze mid-concerto, walked offstage, and never played again — because Margriet, in the front row, mouthed one word: 'Enough.' He begins to understand his collapse was engineered. Emotional beat: shame reframing itself as betrayal.

chapters.title: Anouk's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Anouk (single chapter shift). Anouk confesses: Margriet destroyed Tomas's career first, then Edmund's, sacrificing children to protect the dynasty's myth — and Anouk let it happen to keep Edmund safe from worse. Emotional beat: a mother's guilt laid bare; duty revealed as its own kind of violence.

chapters.title: The Locksmith
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Margriet's will surfaces with a condition: the house passes intact only if the music room is opened within thirty days of her death, or everything goes to the conservatory. Time pressure mounts as Anouk begs Edmund to walk away. Emotional beat: rising dread — the family's silence has a deadline.

chapters.title: Inside the Music Room
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. They break the lock. Inside: Tomas's compositions, unperformed, and evidence of Margriet's theft of his work. Ilse finds her father's handwriting addressed to a daughter he never met. Edmund sits at the piano inside. Emotional beat: catharsis and fury entwined — the truth is both wound and gift.

chapters.title: Vandenberg
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At a small gathering in the reopened house, Edmund performs Tomas's sonata publicly for the first time, signing the program 'E. Vandenberg Reyes.' He signs the house over to Ilse; Anouk, present, weeps without apologizing. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance reclaimed not as property but as voice, freely given.
